name: Glendo State Park (Sagebrush Campground)
note: Sagebrush spreads along about a quarter mile of Glendo Reservoir's south shore in four groups of sites; the turn off Glendo Park Road is easy to miss. Sites 1 and 2 sit on open ground a short walk from the beach; the rest lie among or behind the band of cottonwoods along the shore, and when the reservoir is drawn down the water recedes across bare flats. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: reserve.wyoming.gov (US eDirect API wyordr.usedirect.com/wyomingrdr/rdr/, PlaceId 10 'Glendo State Park', FacilityId 342 'Sagebrush', facility point 42.47130556,-104.986725, read 2026-11-20): 20 web-bookable camping units - 18 'Campsite Non-Electric' SB01-SB08, SB10-SB17, SB19, SB20 (IsRVSite true; Rate 10.00; MaximumStay 14; 'Unit & Parking Size(ft)': SB20 220, SB15/SB19 115, SB14 100, SB01/SB02 95, SB17 80, SB10 75, SB13 70, SB11 60, SB04-SB08/SB16 50, SB03/SB12 45; pull-throughs SB01, SB02, SB10-SB15, SB19, SB20; gravel pads, SB03 and SB20 paved ADA) + Group Sites G09 (225 ft pull-through) and G18 (250 ft back-in), 3 camping units each; plus a day-use shelter SDS -> real drive-in RV campground; every individual site is 45 ft or longer, so a 23-ft rig fits all of them. Wyoming State Parks' own Sagebrush page (wyoparks.wyo.gov/index.php/about-our-campgrounds/1703-sagebrush-glendo, read as search-result text 2026-11-20; the site refuses with an F5 challenge) and its copies on The Dyrt, Campflare and CamplinQ (read 2026-11-20): 'Sagebrush is a low-lying campground which is spread out over a 1/4 mile of the southern lakeshore, and connects with Shelter Point and Whiskey Gulch campgrounds. Sagebrush has 20 developed sites, which are located in 4 separate areas'; 'The first area consists of sites 1 and 2, which are large pull-through sites, with little to no shade and excellent walking access to the beach'; 'Sites 3 through 9 make up the next area, along with one vault toilet'; 'The next area consists of sites 10 through 17, one water hydrant, and one vault toilet'; 'Site 9 is a group site, which will accommodate up to 3 camping units'. No 4WD, sand or rig-size wording on the park text (unlike 15 Broken Arrow / 15742 Red Hills); The Dyrt: 'Access requires a turn at the boat ramp that isn't well-marked from the main road' (a 2025-10-29 review: 'You have to turn at the whiskey boat ramp to get to this campground from the main road'). Imagery 2026-11-20: gravel roads and a loop of pull-through spurs (SB10-SB17), a group circle (G18), a pavilion and toilet buildings. Not in the DB: no WY 'Sagebrush' name match; nearest entries 13969 Custer Cove 1.7 km N (a separate facility across the bay) and 6352 Two Moon 2.5 km E (its own facility at the dam end); Shelter Point (FacilityId 345, lead 22) lies ~0.4 km east of SB01 and Whiskey Gulch (FacilityId 349, lead 24) ~1.2 km west of SB20, each its own engine facility. Public (state): no price gate.
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-20: Esri World Imagery and USGS 3DEP (elevation.nationalmap.gov 3DEPElevation exportImage, F32) fetched in the identical EPSG:3857 square frame at 480 m (0.87 m/px) and 110-150 m (0.22-0.30 m/px) half-widths, with every reserve.wyoming.gov unit point (grid MapInfo, FacilityId 342) plotted and the full-pool contour drawn; all images rendered. Imagery is drawn down (the shore 40-100 m lakeward of the full-pool line). Glendo full pool 4635.0 ft = 1413.51 m NAVD88 (glendo_notes.txt); lidar hydro-flattened water 1412.98 m. Unit points (lidar m) and nearest full-pool crossing of the connected reservoir surface: SB01 1415.0, 18 m (NE); SB02 1415.7, 16 m (NW/N); SB03 1416.9, 19 m; SB04 1415.6, 7 m; SB05 1415.0, 5 m; SB06 1414.4, 5 m; SB07 1413.8, 2 m; SB08 1413.7, 5 m; G09 1415.2, 9 m; SB10-SB12 1416.1-1417.6, 17-20 m; SB13-SB15 1417.4-1418.9, 47-52 m; SB16 1415.3, 25 m; SB17 1417.0, 39 m; G18 1416.3, 29 m; SB19 1415.0, 30 m; SB20 1415.5, 35 m. Ground check: SB01 and SB02 (the first area, east of the peninsula) are gravel pull-throughs on open bare ground with a few scattered single snags running down past the full-pool line to a pale open beach - no treeline, road, berm or day-use strip between; park text: 'sites 1 and 2 ... excellent walking access to the beach'. SB03-SB08 back into the inland edge of a dense, continuous cottonwood stand that lines a narrow inlet west of the peninsula: the full-pool line runs 2-7 m from SB04-SB08 but inside the trees, so at high water the lake stands among the trunks with the open inlet ~30-40 m away through the stand -> filtered view (15741 Mule Hill / 15740 Indian Point precedent). G09 (group) sits in a gravel clearing at the peninsula tip ringed by brush and trees. SB10-SB17, G18, SB19 and SB20 lie behind a continuous cottonwood band 30-100 m deep -> view through trees at most. -> two clear waterfront sites (SB01, SB02) within ~20 m of full pool over open ground -> lakefront with a caveat naming them (few-clear-sites rule, AWH 2026-11-10); the drawdown apron counts because these pads sit at the full-pool line (13969 Custer Cove precedent). Engine tags every Sagebrush unit 'Waterfront Setting: Reservoir' (type-level). Not below the dam: the long embankment south of the campground road has the campground on its reservoir side.

flags: Waterfront lakefront on two sites only (SB01, SB02): unit points 16-18 m from the full-pool contour over open bare ground with a few scattered snags, and the park's own text gives them 'excellent walking access to the beach'. Two sites is at the low end of the few-clear-sites rule (Red Hills had five); lakeview is the fallback if the reviewer wants more than two. SB04-SB08 are closer to the full-pool line (2-7 m) but it runs inside a dense cottonwood stand (Mule Hill precedent: buffer -> view).
SB07 and SB08 stand only 0.2-0.3 m above full pool on lidar (1413.8 / 1413.7 m vs 1413.51 m), so the reservoir near full pool may reach them; no park wording found on high water at Sagebrush.

Pin kept at the engine facility point (by SB04 at the base of the peninsula, the middle of the campground): the unit centroid falls in the narrow inlet west of the peninsula. The campground spreads ~750 m from SB01 (east) to SB20 (west). elevation_meters is Open-Meteo's 1414 m at the pin; lidar puts the units at 1413.7-1418.9 m.
The engine's day-use shelter SDS has a MapInfo point ~1.4 km NW (42.47911,-105.00072), away from the pavilion imaged by G18/SB19; ignored (day use).
